existing.description: The Etta Gray Memorial Scholarship Program, administered by the United Negro College Fund, provides a one-time USD 5,000 need-based scholarship award to students who have a permanent residence in upstate South Carolina and who are pursuing a technical certification at a two-year or four-year college or university in Upstate South Carolina. It was established in honour of the memory of Etta Gray, a loving caregiver for the William Hipp family. UNCF describes itself as the nation's largest private scholarship provider to minority group members and states it awards more than USD 62 million in scholarships each year to students at more than 600 schools. The programme is open on 2026-10-04 with a published deadline of October 30.
eligibility: Permanent residence in upstate South Carolina
Pursuing a technical certification at a two-year or four-year college or university in Upstate South Carolina
Demonstrates financial need, since the award is described as a need-based scholarship
existing.eligibility_summary: Students who have a permanent residence in upstate South Carolina and are pursuing a technical certification at a two-year or four-year college or university located in Upstate South Carolina. The award is need-based and one-time.
benefits: Access to UNCF's scholarships, internships and programmes portal
coverage: One-time USD 5,000 need-based award towards study at a two-year or four-year college or university in Upstate South Carolina
requirements: Submit the UNCF application for this programme before the October 30 deadline
UNCF states that an applicant is not considered for a scholarship, internship or programme until all information and essays required by the application are submitted
application_method: Online application through the UNCF Scholarships, Programs, Internships and Fellowships portal
All required information and essays must be submitted for the application to be considered
existing.selection_notes: UNCF states on its scholarships page: 'Remember: Complete all steps for the applications! You will not be considered for a scholarship, internship or program until you submit all the information and essays the application requires.'
existing.best_fit: Students with a permanent residence in upstate South Carolina who are pursuing a technical certification at a two-year or four-year college or university in Upstate South Carolina and who have financial need.
existing.notes: This programme is one of the awards administered through UNCF's national and regional scholarship portfolio. UNCF states it has helped more than 550,000 students earn their college degrees since its founding, awards more than USD 62 million in scholarships each year, and lists October-closing opportunities on its scholarships page. The individual award amount and October 30 deadline are published by UNCF as the programme's Scholarship of the Month entry for the 2026-2027 cycle.
existing.duration: One-time award for the certification or degree programme in progress
existing.application_period: Applications for the 2026-2027 programme close on October 30; applications are open on 2026-10-04
existing.program_type: Need-based scholarship from a non-governmental organisation

existing.description: The Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program was established by Tony Signore and funded by the Signore Family to support students attending accredited historically black colleges and universities nationwide. UNCF administers and manages the programme for 20 years, through academic year 2038-39. Each year the programme awards two USD 10,000 scholarships to exceptional HBCU seniors who have demonstrated high academic achievement, strong leadership skills, a commitment to community service and unmet financial need. Applicants must hold a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale and must complete a Free Application for Federal Student Aid. The programme is recurring and the next application session has not yet opened on the official page.
eligibility: Enrolled full time as a rising senior at any accredited public or private four-year HBCU
Minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale, verified by submission of a current transcript
Demonstrates a commitment to community service
Demonstrates a demonstrated, unmet financial need as verified by the college or university
Completes a Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) form
existing.eligibility_summary: Rising seniors enrolled full time at any accredited public or private four-year historically black college or university, with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale verified by transcript, a commitment to community service, a demonstrated unmet financial need verified by the college or university, and a completed Free Application for Federal Student Aid.
benefits: Recognition as a Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholar at an HBCU
coverage: USD 10,000 scholarship award supporting study at an accredited four-year HBCU
requirements: Submit a current transcript showing a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5 on a 4.0 scale
Complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid
Have the college or university verify the unmet financial need
Submit all application materials by the deadline once the next session opens
documents: Current transcript evidencing a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or above on a 4.0 scale
College or university verification of unmet financial need
Evidence of commitment to community service as requested by the application
application_method: Online application, with a link to be added to the UNCF programme page when the next session opens
All application materials must be received by the deadline
existing.selection_notes: The programme recognises outstanding young women and men attending HBCUs who have demonstrated high academic achievement, strong leadership skills, commitment to community service and unmet financial need.
existing.best_fit: Rising seniors at an accredited four-year HBCU with a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or above, verified financial need and a record of community service.
existing.notes: The programme was announced in 2018 to mark the bicentennial of Frederick Douglass's birth and is administered and managed by UNCF for 20 years, through academic year 2038-39. UNCF has published recipient announcements from Morris College and Xavier University.
existing.duration: Award to an HBCU senior; no renewal terms are described on the official page
existing.application_period: Annual applications open each year through the 2038-39 academic year. The official page states that a link to the online application will be added when the next session opens, and no calendar date for the next session is published.
existing.program_type: Need-based scholarship for HBCU students, administered by a non-governmental organisation
